full_judgment: 8. Mr Mamunur Rashid, learned Counsel, appearing for respondent No.2, on the other hand,  has submitted that the suit wherein the appellant filed the application under Order XIV, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for fixation of total money payable to the Bank at taka 11,50,000 by applying the provisions of section 47 read with section 60 of the Ain, 2003 giving rise to this appeal having been filed prior to coming into force of the Ain, 2003, the Artha Rin Adalat acted within its jurisdiction in passing the Order dated 4-10-2004 challenged in the writ petition and the High Court Division rightly refused to interfere with the same. He has further submitted that the Ain, 2003 came into force on 1st May, 2003 and if the language of section 47 of the Ain, 2003 which came into effect on 1st May, 2004 is carefully gone into it will appear that limitation to claim interest against a debtor by financial institution like the plaintiff-bank exceeding 200% over the actual loan has been imposed only in respect of the suits filed after 1st May, 2004 and the suit in question having been filed long before the coming into force of the said section of the Ain, the appellant cannot demand/charge interest on the actual amount not exceeding 200% and, as such, there being no merits in the contentions raised on behalf of the appellant the appeal be dismissed.
